key_insight: Random-reshuffling SGD can guarantee convergence of the final iterate with a much larger constant stepsize than prior last-iterate results, removing the usual explicit 1/n restriction up to logarithmic factors.
engineering_relevance: This makes RR-SGD more practical for large finite-sum machine learning problems because the naturally returned last model iterate can be used without requiring overly tiny per-component stepsizes.
method: Analyze unconstrained finite-sum optimization with convex, L-smooth component losses.
Retain the sampling bias at random comparison points in the proof to avoid the explicit 1/n stepsize dependence.
Combine the new last-iterate bound with existing small-step results to match averaged-iterate rates up to log factors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an expected objective-gap bound for the RR-SGD last iterate with constant component stepsize η ≲ 1/(L(1 + log(nK))), where K is the number of epochs.
watch_item: The guarantee is logarithmically weakened and applies to unconstrained convex L-smooth finite-sum problems, so its direct use in nonconvex or constrained settings is not implied.
paper_title: Large-Step Last-Iterate Convergence of Random-Reshuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent
